newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO'S SIMEONE FACES COMPLAINT OVER STAMPING INCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO'S SIMEONE FACES COMPLAINT OVER STAMPING INCIDENT.

text.p: Athletic Bilbao have asked the Spanish league to take action against Diego Simeone after the Atletico Madrid midfielder stamped on Julen Guerrero's leg in Sunday's dramatic 1-1 draw between the sides.

The request is supported by video evidence which clearly shows the Argentine international captain digging his studs in after shielding the ball from the Athletic striker, who needed four stitches in a freely-bleeding wound.
Simeone denies having caused the injury intentionally, and criticised Guerrero for making the original challenge.
"If he takes it badly that's his problem," said Simeone, a player with a hard-man reputation who was involved in a similar clash with Guerrero last season.
"The more they insult me, the more I like it," he added.
Athletic club authorities, normally a model of serenity amongst the hysteria surrounding the Spanish game, have reacted strongly.
"Simeone is undesirable in football," said Athletic chairman Jose Maria Arrate, who accepted that the referee had not spotted the incident.
Guerrero, who may miss Spain's World Cup qualifying match with Yugoslavia on Saturday as a result of the injury, has said he may take civil action against the Atletico player.
The controversy, together with several other talking-points from the action-packed game, has threatened to eclipse even the post-mortems for Saturday's big Real Madrid-Barcelona clash.

Atletico coach Radomir Antic hit out at the referee for failing to award his side two penalties, and also attacked his Athletic counterpart Luis Fernandez for ordering the pitch to be watered before kick-off.
"It is an irregularity which must be denounced. If in Bilbao it rains so much, I don't understand why it has to be watered." said Antic, who lost his customary composure after the game.
"Antic cries too much," he said, hinting that there had been incidents between the two coaches in the players' tunnel after the game.
